newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Jan CPI seen poor but better in Feb -Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Jan CPI seen poor but better in Feb -Prodi.

text.p: Inflation data for January will not be good because of statistical reasons, but the figures will improve in February, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday.
"January last year was a strange month and for this reason the data this January will not be excellent. However in February data will be good," Prodi told reporters in this northern Italian city.

National statistics office Istat introduced a new basket of goods to weigh price rises last January and inflation came in at 5.5 percent year-on-year from 5.8 percent in December 1995. No month-on-month figure was given because of the new basket.
Official inflation data for December are due on Wednesday. Provisional figures released late last month pointed to inflation running at between 2.5-2.6 percent year-on-year.
Prodi said that GDP data released by Istat earlier on Tuesday "weren't bad".
Istat said GDP rose 0.7 percent year-on-year in the third quarter and 0.6 percent by comparison with the second quarter. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
